prs.title: fix(nitro): register compat and import protection plugins once
prs.author: onmax
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description With `experimental.nitroViteEnvironment`, `setupNitroCompat` registered the `nuxt:nitro-v2-compat` and `nuxt:nitro-resolve-fallback` plugins twice: once in `nitroConfig.rollupConfig.plugins`, and again as Vite plugins scoped to the `nitro` environment with `applyToEnvironment` Nitro already passes `rollupConfig.plugins` to every server build, including the `nitro` Vite environment. The Vite copies duplicated that, so each `resolveId` ran twice in the nitro environment. repo: https://github.com/onmax/repros/tree/repro/nuxt-nitro-plugins-twice/nuxt-nitro-plugins-twice

prs.title: fix(nuxt): prevent useCookie CookieStore sync from rewriting with refresh
prs.author: FelixFangX
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

Fixes #36656

### ❓ Type of change

- [x] bugfix
- [ ] new feature
- [ ] docs or chore

### 📚 Description

`useCookie(..., { refresh: true, maxAge })` can rewrite the cookie in an endless loop on Chromium once a Cookie Store `change` event arrives (regression since 4.6.0 / #36006).

**Why**

`handleChange` pauses the watcher, assigns `cookie.value`, and resumes on `nextTick`. Vue's native `pause()`/`resume()` still runs a trigger that fired while paused, so the watcher runs again after resume. The watcher calls `callback(opts.refresh)`, and with `refresh: true` that path skips the `isEqual` bail-out and calls `writeClientCookie`. With `maxAge`, each write refreshes expiry → another CookieStore `change` → loop.

**Fix**

Gate `writeClientCookie` with a `syncing` flag while applying an external `handleChange` update (held across resume + an extra `nextTick`). Intentional same-value assignment with `refresh: true` still rewrites as before.

Also noted in the issue thread: @rynx-cc's equality-bail in the `customRef` setter is a related hardening; this PR targets the CookieStore sync path specifically so refresh semantics stay intact for deliberate writes.

### ✅ Tests / evidence

- New unit test in `test/nuxt/composables.test.ts`: a CookieStore `change` must **not** call `document.cookie` setter; assigning the same value with `refresh: true` still writes once.
- Matches the reproduction in https://gist.github.com/ilyaDegtyarenko/050172b2e1c0e7586264022411874
…(truncated)

prs.title: perf(nuxt): encode rendered html chunk by chunk
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 📚 Description if a rendered page contains a single non-Latin1 character (e.g `→`), V8 has to store the whole joined document as a two-byte string, which makes encoding it to UTF-8 much slower. for a ~250KB document, time spent after the Vue render: | | main | branch | delta | | - | - | - | - | | ASCII only | 324µs | 450µs | +39% | | one `→` | 870µs | 498µs | -43% | this PR keeps Vue's SSR output as the chunks it was rendered in, and in a happy path, where nothing modifies the rendered html, writes each chunk into a reuseable buffer (which is capped at 4MB). if something does change the body, we fall back to joining and `createResponse` as before... there is a small cost for an ASCII-only page, but it's a small fraction of a ~4ms render and pages without a single non-Latin1 character are the minority.

prs.title: fix(nuxt): defer app scope cleanup on external navigation
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue resolves #36659 ### 📚 Description previously we stopped the app scope before assigning the new location, which removed head entries while the old page was still visible (e.g. during a slow redirect) the scope cleanup now runs on `pagehide`, when the page is actually unloading. external navigations that never unload the page (downloads, 204 responses, same-document hashes) also no longer leave the app with a stopped scope either.

prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description this makes it possible to run nuxt typechecking incrementally, by configuring a `tsBuildInfoFile` which can be used by `nuxt typecheck` or by other integrations. the path is in `.nuxt`, doesn't do anything if incremental mode isn't enabled

prs.title: perf(vite): skip tokenising modules without decorators
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description when experimental decorators are enabled, we simply check for `@` before tokenising the module. that's _fine_ but it's very loose and over-parses. (it catches every import from a scoped library, e.g. `import { isArray } from '@vue/shared'`, for example) this improves the regexp filter to rule out modules which cannot contain a decorator testing on `test/fixtures/basic`: | | modules tokenised | time per pass | | --- | --- | --- | | before | 102 | 8.8 ms | | after | 3 | 0.18 ms | | delta | -97% | -98% | the three remaining are the one module with a real decorator and two with `// @ts-expect-error` (which we keep for the sake of all righteousness)

prs.title: fix(nuxt): only match hydration modifiers after lazy prefix
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description when both `Line.vue` and `TimeLine.vue` exist, `` renders `Line`. the same happens for any component whose name starts with a hydration strategy... this PR fixes the regexp...

prs.title: fix(nuxt): avoid hoisting setup-only values from `definePageMeta`
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description if a page passes a setup-only value into `definePageMeta`, every route in the app 500s, not just that page. something like this: ```vue ``` this PR adds some better DX around that, by checking what would be hoisted, and if it would throw because it access the setup state. when we can't tell (e.g. calling a function directly in the meta), we wrap it in a small try/catch to avoid a 500 over the entire app.

prs.title: feat(nuxt): `timeout` + `signal` for `onNuxtReady`
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description this adds a timeout for `onNuxtReady` so it's possible to ensure that it's not delayed arbitrarily - this was actually because I was running a test in headless chromium which delayed this by over 6s 😭 it also adds a `signal` option so a pending callback can be skipped, e.g. when a component unmounts before the app is ready. I think this should let `@nuxt/scripts` drop its own `disposed` flag in `createNuxtReadyScriptTrigger` (cc: @harlan-zw) ```ts const controller = new AbortController() onNuxtReady(() => { /* ... */ }, { timeout: 2000, signal: controller.signal }) onBeforeUnmount(() => controller.abort()) ```

prs.author: danielroe

prs.title: perf(nuxt): defer the prefetch connection listener until work is held
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description this came out of profiling a Nuxt UI marketing page... creating the prefetch scheduler reads `navigator.connection` to attach a `change` listener, and as it's created in plugin setup that adds ~0.7ms before hydration, even though nothing is scheduled until afterwards. the listener only matters once the connection has actually held work back

prs.title: perf(nuxt): optimise nuxt link ssr rendering
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description this PR includes two improvements to the SSR of NuxtLink first, we can totally skip expensive router.resolve calls when we know a link cannot be active (this only really makes a difference on apps with lots of routes - it would be unnoticeable in small apps) ... and second, we can render vanilla NuxtLinks directly into the ssr buffer as they don't need an instance. in an app with 300 routes, and a page rendering 500 links, this was the measured improvement: | commit | links | before | after | change | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1: skip route resolution | target matches no route | 5.32 | 2.28 | -57% | | 1: skip route resolution | target matches another route | 3.75 | 2.21 | -41% | | 2: render into the SSR buffer | target matches no route | 2.28 | 1.20 | -47% | | 2: render into the SSR buffer | target matches another route | 2.21 | 1.11 | -50% |

prs.title: fix(nitro): preserve wildcard tails in case-insensitive route rules
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description with `router.options.sensitive: false`, a wildcard redirect like `'/old/**': { redirect: '/new/**' }` returns `400` for `/OLD/A/b` with Nitro, while `/old/A/b` redirects correctly. wildcard proxies are affected too. this PR uses the request's spelling of the matched base for redirects and proxies, so the tail keeps its casing and query string.

prs.title: perf(vite): emit v8 compile hints for initial chunks
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body: ### 🔗 Linked issue ### 📚 Description this is one of several PRs from profiling the client side of a Nuxt UI marketing page. most of the hydration cost was V8 lazily compiling functions on the main thread the first time they ran. so, this PR adds a [V8 explicit compile hint](https://v8.dev/blog/explicit-compile-hints) (`//# allFunctionsCalledOnLoad`) to the top of the entry, layout and page chunks, plus anything they statically import. Chrome 136+ then compiles those chunks eagerly, off the main thread, while it streams them. other browsers ignore the comment. | | before | after | | - | - | - | | hydration (Playwright, CPU x8) | 477ms | 311ms | | TBT on load | 137ms | 40ms | | longest task | 187ms | 90ms | | Lighthouse TBT | 87ms | 55ms |

prs.title: feat(nuxt): resolve template components in the vue compiler
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

resolves #31604
closes #36446

### 📚 Description

this resolves auto-imported components inside the Vue template compiler via a custom `nodeTransforms` entry, rather than recovering them from the compiled output afterwards.

this node transform now does three things for `.vue` templates, all of which are more performant and reduce work in compilation:

| | before | now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `<Foo />` | output rewritten with regex | imported by the template compiler |
| `<LazyFoo hydrate-on-visible />` | renamed in SFC | strategy read in the same pass |
| `<ClientOnly>` + `.client` slots | output re-parsed with oxc | removed from the AST before codegen |

the transform can't edit `<script setup>`, so we record which setup bindings were removed from the template, and we drop them in `TreeShakeTemplatePlugin` if nothing else references them.

we still need the components loader plugin to handle `resolveComponent('X')` in scripts and `h(X)` in JSX.

lazy, client-only and server components are imported from small per-importer virtual modules to keep chunking the same as it is today.

because it runs on the compiled template AST, we now don't care how the template was written, so `<template lang="pug">` now supports lazy hydration props 🎉

many thanks to @CloudNine13 for the pug fixture pages and e2e coverage, taken from #36446 ❤️

on the generated large app from `test/bench/large-app.ts`, it's not just more correct; it's also a little faster:

prs.title: fix(nitro,vite): dedupe dev css by module node
prs.author: saini-25
prs.body:
Resolves #36392
closes https://github.com/nuxt/nuxt/pull/36421

In dev mode, Vite was registering both `/@fs` and bare path URLs for layer CSS, which caused `collectDevCss` to generate duplicate stylesheet links. The duplicate CSS could appear after the app's CSS and override its styles.
Fixed this by deduplicating entries in `collectDevCss` using seen module nodes while preserving the first URL. Added unit tests in `packages/vite/test/css.test.ts`.

prs.title: fix(nitro,vite): remove windows + virtual dev ssr css links after hydration
prs.author: danielroe
prs.body:
### 🔗 Linked issue

resolves #36737

### 📚 Description

since 4.6.2, on Windows, global CSS outside `srcDir` keeps its SSR `<link>` after hydration, so it loads twice and the stale link sits ahead of the injected `<style>` tags, breaking cascade layer order.

this is because windows drive letters are treated as non-path ids, so instead we now link absolute paths through `/@fs/`

additionally, we now remove the `/@id/` link for virtual CSS, which likely had the same problem since #36549, and no just on windows.
